steps.title: Muscadet
steps.body: Melon grows almost only in the Pays Nantais, near Nantes, where the Loire meets the Atlantic. Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, the largest and most important appellation, sits south-east of Nantes. Muscadet Coteaux de la Loire and Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu are smaller. The climate is maritime: mild, damp, with sea breezes.

steps.title: Crus communaux
steps.body: Since 2011, Muscadet has recognised crus communaux, village crus, with specific soils and longer lees ageing, from 17 months to several years. Examples include Clisson, on granite, Gorges, on gabbro, and Le Pallet, on gneiss and gabbro. They show Melon's capacity for complex, age-worthy wines.

steps.prompt: Match each cru to its soil.

steps.body: Look for a cru communal name on a Muscadet label. These wines spend much longer on their lees and show how serious Melon can be.

options: Village crus with specific soils and long lees ageing
steps.explanation: They require specific soils and extended lees ageing.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Melon grows in the Pays Nantais, mainly Sèvre et Maine
The climate is maritime and mild
Crus communaux, since 2011, show its complexity
